title: Il Discorso Indiretto
subtitle: Reporting what someone said, and how the tenses shift back.
objectives: Convert direct speech into reported speech with dire che
Shift tenses back correctly when the reporting verb is in the past
Adjust pronouns, possessives and time expressions appropriately

content.intro: Reporting what someone said requires more than just adding "that" — pronouns, tenses and time expressions often all need to shift to fit the new perspective.
content.explanation: When the reporting verb (dire, chiedere, rispondere) is in the present, little changes besides pronouns. When it's in the past — by far the more common case in real narration — every tense in the reported clause shifts one step back: present → imperfetto, passato prossimo → trapassato prossimo, futuro → condizionale passato (a form met at C1; condizionale presente is an acceptable simplification at this level).

rules.heading: a) Also shift: pronouns, possessives, time words
rules.body:
• domani → il giorno dopo; oggi → quel giorno; ieri → il giorno prima
  • qui → lì; questo → quello
  • Subject/possessive pronouns adjust to the new speaker's perspective

rules.heading: b) Imperative becomes di + infinitive
rules.body: Direct: "Chiudi la porta!" Reported: Mi ha detto di chiudere la porta.

examples.it: Marco ha detto: "Sono stanco." → Marco ha detto che era stanco.
examples.en: Marco said: "I'm tired." → Marco said he was tired.

examples.it: Ha detto: "Verrò domani." → Ha detto che sarebbe venuto il giorno dopo.
examples.en: He said: "I'll come tomorrow." → He said he would come the next day.

examples.it: Mi ha chiesto: "Hai finito?" → Mi ha chiesto se avevo finito.
examples.en: She asked me: "Have you finished?" → She asked me if I had finished.

examples.it: "Aspetta qui!" → Mi ha detto di aspettare lì.
examples.en: "Wait here!" → She told me to wait there.

commonMistakes.wrong: Ha detto che è stanco. (reporting from a past viewpoint)
commonMistakes.why: A past reporting verb (ha detto) shifts the present tense of direct speech back to the imperfetto.

commonMistakes.wrong: Mi ha detto "chiudi la porta" as reported speech kept verbatim
commonMistakes.right: Mi ha detto di chiudere la porta.
commonMistakes.why: The imperative in direct speech becomes di + infinitive when reported, never kept as a literal imperative.

items.prompt: Ha detto: "Sto lavorando." → Ha detto che ___.
items.explanation: Present → imperfetto after a past reporting verb.

items.prompt: Ha detto: "Ho finito il lavoro." → Ha detto che ___.

items.explanation: Futuro shifts to the conditional, and domani shifts to il giorno dopo.

summary: A past reporting verb shifts tenses back: presente→imperfetto, passato prossimo→trapassato prossimo, futuro→condizionale.
Pronouns, possessives and time expressions (domani→il giorno dopo) shift to the new perspective too.
A reported imperative becomes di + infinitive.
